_what: Lines the gate EXPECTS to see repeating (#2848). Each entry is a regex over the NORMALISED line (numbers -> N, timestamps -> T, shas -> H; see normaliseLine in repeating-lines.ts -- so `a11ign` reads `aNign`) and carries the reason. An entry without a reason is refused at load.
_rule: Add an entry only for a line that is the org working as designed. A line that reports a fault is fixed or filed `ready`; it is never allowlisted to make the offer stop.

allow.reason: wake.ts's report of an order whose seat is mid-turn (#3029): the queue waiting for a turn to end, which it exists to do. It is written until the seat is idle and carries its own age; past one hour (BUSY_SEAT_DEFERRAL_MS) the order is written as UNDELIVERED with the `nowhere to go` summary instead, and neither of those is allowlisted.

work the gate can see and is deliberately not offering (a declared blockedBy, Not-before, answer: or a file overlap with an open pull request); a row in a keyed repository is printed with its key (`agent-org#460`), the same state. The line itself says it clears itself; 972 per day measured on 2026-10-01 and each is a row waiting on a field.

blocking-impact.ts's readout of a holder that shelves 1 to 4 rows, printed for every holder every tick (`holdingLines`): the count, the rows it shelves, and, after `behind`, the rows it is held behind. Below BLOCKING_MIN_ROWS (5) it is a count that has its own threshold and owner and is not a fault: a ready row held behind an open pull request in review for an hour repeats this line for as long as the review takes (agent-org#818, measured 2026-10-11: one holder, 59 consecutive ticks). A keyed row (`agent-org#N`) is the same state, as the SHELVED entry's. The FAULT form of the same count is an incident at 5 rows for 30 minutes: it carries `(episode open)` and is recorded in the failure ledger, and that form is NOT allowlisted, nor is a line with no row list, nor the `N B4 shelvings` line.

update-tool.ts states where the tool's own checkout is on every tick it runs (the work-tick unit's first ExecStartPre); it is a position reading, the twin of the primary's line below, and was offered to orchestrator after 30 ticks on 2026-10-02. A failed update throws and prints a different line (`has uncommitted changes to tracked files`, `is not a primary checkout`), which is not allowlisted.

the tick's version banner (a11ign/a11ign#3443): update-tool.ts prints `agent-org vX.Y.Z (<sha>)` and work-tick.ts prints `agent-org vX.Y.Z` on EVERY tick so a journal read says which release made each decision. It is a position reading, the twin of the checkout lines below, and 37 consecutive ticks of it were offered to orchestrator on 2026-10-04 (a11ign/a11ign#3497). The faulting forms print different lines, `agent-org (at no release tag: <sha>)` and `agent-org (version unreadable: ...)`, and neither is allowlisted.

the gate's reading of githubstatus.com, written on EVERY tick (work-gate.ts `holdForIncidentNow`, a11ign/a11ign#3723) so the cost of the call is in the journal: the CLEAR state, the one it is in whenever GitHub has no incident. It is a position reading, the twin of the version banner, and 30 consecutive ticks of it were offered to orchestrator on 2026-10-06. The other two states print different lines, `github-status: UNKNOWN (...)` (the status page could not be read) and `GITHUB INCIDENT: ...` (a runner outage is holding orders), and neither is allowlisted.
update-primary.ts states where the checkout is on every tick it runs; it is a position reading, not a fault. A failed update prints a different line, which is not allowlisted.

the package manager's echo of the ExecStartPre command, written on every tick by the runner itself. npm printed `> name@version script`; pnpm, which the tick unit runs since a11ign/a11ign#2974's cut-over 3, appends the checkout path (`... primary:update /home/agent/repos/a11y-witness`), and the entry's `$` anchor rejected that form: 75 consecutive ticks were offered to orchestrator on 2026-10-02. The SECOND line pnpm prints is the script body: `node packages/agent-org/src/update-primary.ts` until a11ign/a11ign#3097's cut-over 4, `agent-org primary:update` since, and that body was offered after 30 ticks on 2026-10-03.

allow.pattern: ^claim-stall: tracker `\S+` \(\S+\): N claimed rows, N evaluated\.$
allow.reason: work-gate/claim-stall-tick.ts's count of a keyed tracker's claimed rows and of the ones the pass evaluated (agent-org#941), printed once per keyed tracker per tick while it holds a claimed row. It is a position reading, the twin of the version banner and the checkout lines: the count changes with the rows (3 to 11 measured on 2026-10-11) and normaliseLine turns every number to N, so one line repeated for 30 ticks was offered to orchestrator as a fault. The faulting forms are NOT allowlisted and print their own lines: `... -- not evaluated.` (a row it cannot read, or one that carries no session label), `... -- its claimed rows were NOT evaluated this tick (UNREAD ...)` (a tracker it cannot read), `NO claim was evaluated this tick` (comments it cannot read), `is HELD, not released`, and `claim-stall: could not run (...)`.

allow.pattern: ^gate-rest: N of N conditional reads answered N$
allow.reason: src/work-gate/tick.ts's tickReadingLines (a11ign/a11ign#5169), printed on EVERY tick the gate runs with the conditional-read flag on: `gate-rest: N of N conditional reads answered 304`, how many of the gate's REST list reads came back `304 Not Modified` and were answered from the kept body (the ETag cache working). It is the figure the live hour is measured from, so it repeats by design, and the count moves with the reads while normaliseLine turns every number to N. A refused read prints a different tail, which is not allowlisted.

allow.pattern: ^read memo: N identical read\(s\) answered from memory, N distinct answer\(s\) held at the end of the tick\.$
allow.reason: src/work-gate/reads.ts's exit line (agent-org#1095), written as the gate's process ends on every tick it runs: an identical read made again within the tick is answered from the memory the process holds, not asked of `gh` a second time (read deduplication working). A refused read is never kept, so it is never counted as a hit here, and a different tail of the line is not allowlisted.

allow.pattern: ^(PARTIAL: N lane\(s\) skipped by pacing, none refused: .*|lane\(s\) skipped by pacing, none refused; see the gate's stderr)$
allow.reason: the gate's PARTIAL line and the tick's reading of it when every unread lane was SKIPPED BY DESIGN (agent-org#1414): `gate.graphqlPacing` below the pool's reserve, or an event-gated webhook tick that no event named a repository on and whose last whole read is under GRAPHQL_SWEEP_MINUTES old (`pacedSkips`, `unreadLanes`). Nothing was refused and the gate exits PACED (4), not PARTIAL (3); 663 consecutive ticks of it were offered to orchestrator as a fault on 2026-10-14/15. It is a position reading, the twin of the version banner and the checkout lines. The REFUSED form is NOT allowlisted and prints a different line: `PARTIAL: could not read ...` from the gate and `one lane could not be read; see the gate's stderr` from the tick, which a refusal in ANY lane still produces, paced lanes alongside or not.
systemd's per-run resource accounting line, written after every tick.
